title: POC capacity sizing + burst/fallback scoping - StellarNet
transcript:
--- Meeting Header ---
Date: 2025-06-18
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Cole (Redwood AE); Priya Narang (Redwood SE); Ravi Patel (StellarNet - CTO); Lena Gomez (StellarNet - Head of ML); Marcus Liu (StellarNet - Infra)

Summary:
StellarNet wants a 4-week POC to validate inference economics and latency under bursty traffic. Success criteria: p95 latency <= 250ms for single-turn chat at production mix, cost per 1M tokens below their threshold, and graceful degradation when capacity exhausted. Plan: reserved baseline GPUs (2x A100 equiv), burst pool for traffic spikes, automated fallback to quantized 70B model and regional fallback. Run three benchmarks (baseline steady, burst ramp, failure/fallback) with synthetic and replayed production traces.

Topics:
- workload sizing and traffic profile
- reserved vs burst capacity
- autoscaling and queueing policies
- fallback model variants and routing policies
- benchmarks and metrics to capture
- timeline and success criteria

Action items (in call):
- See action items section near end for owners and dates.

Transcript:
[00:00] Ethan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick ice breaker — you sent the traffic patterns, Marcus? I had a look.
[00:20] Marcus (StellarNet - Infra): Yeah, shared in the doc, it's pretty spiky, we get 20 qps steady, then bursts up to 2k for 30-90s when feature flag toggles on. That's the thing we need to validate.
[01:10] Priya (Redwood SE): Cool. So from Redwood's side we typically size a reserved pool to cover steady-state plus a safety buffer for sustained spikes and then enable a burst pool that uses preemptible or shared capacity for short surges. For the POC we recommended 2 reserved GPUs as a baseline.
[02:05] Ravi (CTO): Two GPUs — is that A100s? What's the expected p95 at that size? Our app is latency sensitive, our goal is p95 < 250ms for single-turn retrieval-augmented replies.
[02:30] Priya: We tested similar workloads — on A100-equivalent with batching tuned for your token distribution we can hit p95 ~180-220ms at 15-20 rps for the 13B model. For the 70B it's higher, so the plan is: reserved pool for mid-size model (13B quantized), burst pool can serve larger models but we fallback to smaller/quantized variants if latency rises.
[03:10] Lena (Head of ML): Our primary model is a 70B LLM right now; we can run a quantized 13B equivalent for POC if it changes quality too much. Need to see quality delta metrics.
[04:00] Priya: We'll run A/B style quality checks during the benchmarks; we'll capture rouge-like metrics, hallucination rates on a set of prompts you give us.
[05:00] Ethan: Important note — burst strategy: Redwood can pre-warm instances using a burst credit model so there's not a cold-start spike. But if burst pool saturated we'll do policy-based fallback: first route to smaller quantized model (fastest); then regional fallback; then queue with token-based prioritization. We'll record the switchovers and latencies.
[06:20] Marcus: What about autoscaling latency and buffer settings? If we autoscale purely on GPU utilization it's often too slow for 30-90s spikes.
[06:45] Priya: Exactly. We use hybrid autoscaling: scale on queue length and request rate signals plus predictive warm-up based on feature flag telemetry you can send. For short spikes we rely on burst capacity and pre-warmed instances — autoscale kicks in for sustained increases (minutes), not seconds.
[07:30] Ravi: Cost question — how much will burst cost vs reserved? We need ballpark to decide reserved commit.
[07:50] Ethan: For the POC we'll give you pricing scenarios: reserved baseline (2 GPUs) monthly equivalent pro-rated for test period, burst per-minute pricing, and a blended cost per 1M tokens estimate. I'll send that by Friday.
[08:20] Lena: Benchmarks — what exact tests will you run?
[08:40] Priya: Three tests: 1) steady-state at 20 rps for 1 hour to validate throughput; 2) synthetic burst ramp: drive from 20 to 2k rps over 30s hold for 90s then drop; 3) failure-mode: intentionally saturate reserved + burst to validate fallbacks and quality under fallback.
[09:20] Marcus: We'll provide a 48-hour anonymized trace of production traffic and a 200-prompt eval set. Also we want end-to-end latency measured from our edge.
[10:00] Priya: Perfect. We'll run both synthetic replay and your trace replay so results are comparable.
[11:00] Ethan: Success criteria recap: p95 <= 250ms for at least 95% of the steady+typical bursts; fallback quality acceptable per your eval thresholds; cost below your threshold X dollars per 1M tokens. Also no data exfiltration concerns — we'll enable KMS and audit logs for the POC.
[12:10] Ravi: About security: SOC2 is fine, but we need SSO and RBAC for team access during POC.
[12:40] Ethan: We'll provide our security pack, SSO via SAML, and you can restrict Console to allowlist. I'll attach the SOC2 report and admin roles doc.
[13:10] Lena: One subtle thing — our requests include long KV cache prefixes sometimes 1k tokens, does your runtime handle KV cache eviction gracefully?
[13:40] Priya: Yes, but note the transcript from some internal tests shows 'K-V cash' mis-phrases — but seriously, we manage KV caches and we can tune the cache retention per-model to keep token memory hot; we'll test with your prefix lengths.
[14:30] Marcus: For burst capacity, do you prefer using dedicated reserved burst GPUs or ephemeral cloud GPUs?
[14:50] Priya: For short spikes ephemeral shared GPUs are cost-effective. For longer bursts we can recommend transient reserved (reserved burst credits) or bump the committed pool. We'll show cost models for both.
[16:05] Ethan: Routing policy detail: policy order we propose — 1) primary route to reserved pool on preferred region/model; 2) if reserved saturated, try burst pool in same region; 3) if burst saturated, fallback to quantized variant in same region; 4) if still saturated, route to next region's burst pool; 5) final is queued with token-priority.
[17:10] Ravi: How granular are the fallbacks — model variants per route or global?
[17:30] Priya: Per-route and per-customer you can pin model versions. For the POC we'll configure route-level fallback so web requests for critical flows prioritize latency.
[18:05] Marcus: Observability — we need token-level latency and cost breakdowns, traces per request.
[18:40] Ethan: Redwood Console will expose model-level token breakdowns, P95/P99 latency, fallback events, and a CSV export. We'll also provide a small tracer snippet to inject request IDs.
[19:20] Lena: Timeline — you said 4 weeks, what's the breakdown?
[19:40] Priya: Week 0: prep and provisioning (1-3 days), Week 1: baseline steady-state runs and infra tuning, Week 2: burst tests + evaluations, Week 3: failure-mode and extended runs + report. Buffer 1 week for unexpected. Total 3-5 weeks.
[20:30] Ethan: Benchmarks logs and raw metrics will be uploaded to the shared folder. We recommend a benchmark configuration spreadsheet — I'll share a template.
[21:10] Marcus: Are there any limits for concurrent KV cache size or session affinity for chat?
[21:40] Priya: We can pin sessions to instances to keep KV cache warm; there's tradeoffs with throughput. We'll instrument and decide in early runs.
[22:15] Ravi: If the POC meets criteria, we'll look at reserved commit for production. What's the typical ramp to Dedicated?
[22:35] Ethan: For customers moving to Dedicated we size based on POC peaks and SLA targets — usually a commit for 8-16 GPUs initially depending on traffic. We'll provide a recommendation if POC successful.
[23:10] Lena: Quality regression alarms — can you tie failures to a prompt set?
[23:30] Priya: Yes, Redwood Optimize will run periodic evals and emit alerts if metrics deviate; we'll include that for the POC with your eval set.
[24:05] Speaker 3: (inaud) — sorry dropped for a second — are we capturing cold-start counts during bursts?
[24:25] Priya: Yes we'll log cold starts, pre-warm successes, and time-to-warm.
[25:05] Marcus: What about region preference — our primary users are US-east and EU-west. If eu-west is saturated, do we route to us-east — impact on latency?
[25:40] Ethan: We'll measure cross-region latency and you'll get trade-offs: routing to us-east may add 80-120ms RTT, which could push p95 over target. That's why the quantized fallback is important to keep latency low within region.
[26:30] Lena: For the quality checks, we'll mark certain prompts as high-priority — they should never go to quantized fallback.
[26:50] Priya: We'll tag routes accordingly so high-priority flows are only served from reserved pool and will be queued rather than degraded.
[27:30] Ethan: Next steps and action items we'll put in CRM and share the plan. Quick live recap before close.
[28:00] Ethan: Recap: Redwood to provision 2 reserved GPUs for baseline, enable burst pool, run three benchmark phases including your trace, provide pricing and security docs by Friday, share benchmark template, set up SAML for your team, and instrument request IDs.
[30:15] Ravi: Sounds good. Two favors — can you also run a worst-case cost calc if 10% of traffic hits 70B in bursts?
[30:40] Ethan: Yes we'll include that scenario.
[31:00] Marcus: Any blockers from Redwood side?
[31:15] Priya: Need the anonymized trace, eval prompt set, and an account to push SAML test users.
[31:40] Lena: We'll share those by tomorrow.
[32:00] Ethan: Great. We'll schedule a 30-minute kickoff for provisioning once we confirm dates.
[40:00] (late in call) Priya: small note — when we run replay tests we'll simulate client-side RTT to match your edge so latency numbers reflect real-world.
[45:30] Ethan: Ok thanks everyone, we'll follow up with docs and pricing. Appreciate the clarity on the burst profile.
[51:10] Ravi: Thanks, talk soon.
[51:30] (call ends)

--- End Transcript ---
summary: StellarNet and Redwood scoped a 4-week POC focusing on capacity sizing, burst handling, and fallback policies. Baseline recommended: 2 reserved GPUs with burst pool for short spikes; fallback ordered to quantized model then cross-region then queue. Benchmarks: steady-state, synthetic burst ramp, and failure-mode with replayed production trace. Success criteria: p95 latency <= 250ms for steady+typical bursts, acceptable quality on fallback, and cost within customer threshold. Redwood to provide pricing, security docs, benchmark templates, and set up SAML; StellarNet to provide trace and eval prompts.
